literal_meaning: A ghost pressing on the neck
figurative_meaning_en: Having a sudden mischievous or naughty idea
similar_in_english: The devil made me do it
example_sentences_in_bangla: তার ঘাড়ে ভূত চাপা পড়েছে, তাই সে হঠাৎ এমন দুষ্টুমি করতে শুরু করল।
বাচ্চাটার ঘাড়ে ভূত চাপা, দেখ কীভাবে খেলনা ভাঙছে!
example_sentences_in_english: A ghost has sat on his neck, that's why he's suddenly up to mischief.
The kid has a devilish idea, look how he's breaking the toys!
history: This idiom draws from Bengali folklore where ghosts (bhoot) are believed to sit on people's necks, causing sleep paralysis or influencing bad behavior, rooted in rural superstitions.
note: The idiom reflects cultural beliefs in supernatural influences on human actions, often used humorously in modern contexts.
